title: Broadband Cabin Connectivity Installation with Crown Adapter Plate and Radome
abstract: Fleet retrofit of a high-throughput cabin broadband service on the Evo variants, comprising a fuselage-mounted antenna on a new crown adapter plate, a connectivity server in an existing rack position and wireless coverage from the ceiling void.

sections.reason: A launch operator of both Evo variants has made cabin broadband a condition of contract renewal after losing two corporate travel accounts on the point, and three further operators have asked for the same capability in the same delivery window. The aircraft were delivered with the harness provision but without the equipment, so there is no in-service capability at all today. The commercial case is time-critical rather than technical: the operator wants the first aircraft before the northern winter season and the whole fleet inside eighteen months, and has stated that a drag penalty above one tenth of one per cent block fuel would make the retrofit uneconomic on its sector lengths.
sections.description: A low-profile fuselage-mounted antenna is installed on a new machined adapter plate on the Section 15 crown between frames 44 and 48, faired by a composite radome shaped to the operator's drag requirement. The connectivity server takes the forward seat track cover sub-assembly D4430115773572 as its mounting shelf in the existing overhead rack, and the external communication trim kit D4430003711226 is re-cut where the coaxial run enters. The outboard latch kit INDE528543-55 and the right-hand decor panel assembly QUI1349-94 are re-worked to give tool-free access to the server for line maintenance. Wireless coverage is provided from four access points in the ceiling void at positions 5RK, and the server is addressed at position 6RK with the forward decor panel position 61RM re-labelled. Configuration is held in load LB9L26864CA and the application load LH1L158FBA9 runs on the server. The dependent position determining transceiver D3450007115686, which sits on the same crown between the same frames, is displaced 700 mm aft and its coaxial run is re-made. Work is in zone 293 for the crown and in zones 971 and 974 for the cabin equipment. Detail is on drawing D44300045182.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 148 kg per aircraft including the adapter plate, radome, server and cabling, forward of the reference datum, giving a centre-of-gravity shift of 0.09 per cent MAC that must be recorded. Electrical load increases by 3 200 VA in cruise, which is inside the existing galley bus margin only if the forward galley oven group is load-shed during peak service; that constraint is under review. Drag penalty is estimated at 0.08 per cent block fuel, inside the operator requirement but not yet flight-validated. No revenue seats are lost. Cabin crew gain a reset function on the attendant panel. Wiring content for the crown route, the cabin equipment list and the avionics rack loading chart all require update.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only. Provisional estimate is seven days in a hangar, of which two are the crown adapter plate installation and the radome fit. The adapter plate is the long-lead item at twenty-six weeks. No production cut-in is proposed because the Evo cabin definition is handled through customer options rather than through the standard.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must confirm that the adapter plate footprint does not overlap the reinforced pad already installed for the navigation aerial, that the two installations can be substantiated as a single crown structure rather than sequentially, and whether the galley load-shed constraint is acceptable to the operator.

type_data.balance_impact: Forward of the reference datum; CG shift of 0.09 % MAC, reportable
type_data.production_impact: No cut-in; the Evo cabin definition is handled as a customer option
